page.layout: One page of text, single column, with running head at top; page number at top left. Marginal quotation marks (printed as small double marks) at the start of each line are typographic, not notes. Catchword "qui" at lower right of the text block. Digitiser's watermark at bottom right is excluded.

main_text.p: publicis conventibus & sacris exercitiis, imo & quieti politicæ ab ordinariis laboribus; nam quod caret alternâ requie durabile non est: Is verò per Christum & Apostolos delectus est primus septimanæ, qui dies Solis vulgò dicitur, tàm in memoriam resurrectionis Christi, quàm ad discernendos Christianos à Judæis: Ac sicut hæc praxis fuit continua in Ecclesiâ Christianâ ab Apostolorum obitu, itâ etiàm ab ipsis viventibus fuit introducta, ut patet ex Act. xx, 7. 1 Cor. xv 1, 1, 2. & ipse dies ideò Dominicus per illos appellatus, Apoc. 1, 10. Nec video qui audeant Sociniani omnem quarti Præcepti Moralitatem impugnare, cùm fateantur illius observationem insertam Decalogo, præcipuæ legis parti, quæ cæteroqui ex Moralibus Præceptis tota constat: Sanè non constabit Decalogus totus ex Moralibus Præceptis, si unum ex illis decem merè Ceremoniale fuerit, & nihil Morale ac juris perpetui habuerit. Imò nulla posset fingi ratio, cur streperet anser inter olores, & merè Cerimonialis observatio, inserta fuisset illi parti legis, quæ cætero-qui
[The text is partly obscured by a blue water stain at the lower left; a few words may be uncertain.]

page.notes: Printed quotation marks at line starts are not transcribed. Several words near the blue stain and in the lower left are doubtful, notably "audeant" (the printed word is largely obscured by a smudge and is not clearly legible; treat as [?]) and "streperet" (read as "ftreperet"). Original printing uses long s; rendered as plain s. The page is broken at "cætero-qui", with the catchword "qui" below.
